title: Isaiah Chapter 47 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Isaiah chapter 47 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Isaiah Chapter 47 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Isaiah Chapter 47.

questions.question: Who is addressed to "Come down, and sit in the dust" in Isaiah 47:1?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 47:1 explicitly says, "Come down, and sit in the dust, O virgin daughter of Babylon".

questions.question: What is the virgin daughter of Babylon commanded to do in Isaiah 47:2?
options: Take the millstones, and grind meal
questions.correctAnswer: Take the millstones, and grind meal
questions.explanation: Isaiah 47:2 says, "Take the millstones, and grind meal: uncover thy locks, make bare the leg...".

questions.question: In Isaiah 47:3, what will be uncovered according to the prophecy?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 47:3 states, "Thy nakedness shall be uncovered, yea, thy shame shall be seen."

questions.question: According to Isaiah 47:4, who is the redeemer?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 47:4 declares, "As for our redeemer, the LORD of hosts is his name."

questions.question: What is the daughter of the Chaldeans told to do in Isaiah 47:5?
options: Sit thou silent and get thee into darkness
questions.correctAnswer: Sit thou silent and get thee into darkness
questions.explanation: Isaiah 47:5 says, "Sit thou silent, and get thee into darkness, O daughter of the Chaldeans."

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 47:6 says God was displeased with His people and gave them into the hand of Babylon.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 47:6 states, "I was wroth with my people, I have polluted mine inheritance, and given them into thine hand."

questions.question: True or False: In Isaiah 47:7, the daughter of Babylon remembers the latter end of her reign.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 47:7 says she did not lay these things to her heart, "neither didst remember the latter end of it."

questions.question: According to Isaiah 47:8, what does the daughter of Babylon say in her heart?
options: "I am, and none else beside me"
questions.correctAnswer: "I am, and none else beside me"
questions.explanation: Isaiah 47:8 quotes her saying, "I am, and none else beside me; I shall not sit as a widow."

questions.question: What two things does Isaiah 47:9 say will come upon the daughter of Babylon suddenly?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 47:9 says, "the loss of children, and widowhood: they shall come upon thee in their perfection."

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 47:10 says the daughter of Babylon trusted in her wickedness and said, 'None seeth me.'
questions.explanation: Isaiah 47:10 states, "For thou hast trusted in thy wickedness: thou hast said, None seeth me."

questions.question: What will come upon the daughter of Babylon suddenly according to Isaiah 47:11?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 47:11 says, "and desolation shall come upon thee suddenly."

questions.question: According to Isaiah 47:12, what has the daughter of Babylon labored in from her youth?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 47:12 states, "Stand now with thine enchantments, and with the multitude of thy sorceries, wherein thou hast laboured from thy youth."

questions.question: Who does Isaiah 47:13 challenge to stand up and save the daughter of Babylon?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 47:13 says, "Let now the astrologers, the stargazers, the monthly prognosticators, stand up, and save thee."

questions.question: What will happen to the astrologers and sorcerers according to Isaiah 47:14?
options: They shall be as stubble burned by fire
They shall flee to the mountains
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be as stubble burned by fire
questions.explanation: Isaiah 47:14 says, "Behold, they shall be as stubble; the fire shall burn them."

questions.question: True or False: In Isaiah 47:15, the merchants who helped the daughter of Babylon will save her from destruction.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 47:15 states, "none shall save thee" from those merchants.

medium.title: Isaiah Chapter 47 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Isaiah Chapter 47 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 47:6, why was Babylon given power over God's people?
options: Because God was angry and polluted His inheritance
Because Babylon was stronger and wiser
Because God's people worshipped false gods
Because Babylon was merciful and kind
questions.correctAnswer: Because God was angry and polluted His inheritance
questions.explanation: Isaiah 47:6 states that God was wroth with His people, polluted His inheritance, and gave them into Babylon's hand, highlighting God's displeasure as the reason for Babylon's power, not their mercy or strength.

questions.question: What attitude did Babylon have about its future according to Isaiah 47:7?
options: They believed they would be a lady forever
They feared losing their kingdom soon
They trusted in the LORD of hosts
questions.correctAnswer: They believed they would be a lady forever
questions.explanation: Isaiah 47:7 explains Babylon said, 'I shall be a lady for ever,' showing their arrogance and failure to consider the latter end, which contrasts with trusting God.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 47:8 describe Babylon's lifestyle and self-perception?
options: Given to pleasures and careless, thinking no loss will come
Humble and fearing God, expecting judgment
Diligent in prayer and seeking forgiveness
Generous and kind to the oppressed
questions.correctAnswer: Given to pleasures and careless, thinking no loss will come
questions.explanation: Isaiah 47:8 describes Babylon as given to pleasures, dwelling carelessly, and arrogantly thinking they will not suffer loss or widowhood, illustrating pride and lack of humility.

questions.question: What two calamities does Isaiah 47:9 say will come upon Babylon suddenly?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 47:9 foretells that loss of children and widowhood will come upon Babylon suddenly, as a consequence of their sorceries and enchantments, symbolizing complete desolation.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 47:10 say Babylon trusted in, and what was the result?
options: Trusted in wickedness, which perverted their wisdom
Trusted in the LORD, resulting in peace
Trusted in their armies, gaining victory
questions.correctAnswer: Trusted in wickedness, which perverted their wisdom
questions.explanation: Isaiah 47:10 states Babylon trusted in wickedness and self-deception, claiming 'None seeth me,' but their wisdom and knowledge were perverted, leading to their downfall.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 47:11 describe the coming evil upon Babylon?
options: It will come suddenly and unexpectedly
It will be delayed for many years
It will be easily avoided by prayer
It will be announced by prophets first
questions.correctAnswer: It will come suddenly and unexpectedly
questions.explanation: Isaiah 47:11 emphasizes that evil and desolation will come upon Babylon suddenly and without warning, illustrating the certainty and swiftness of divine judgment.

questions.question: What was Babylon urged to do in Isaiah 47:12 to try to save themselves?
options: Stand with their enchantments and sorceries
Pray to the LORD for mercy
questions.correctAnswer: Stand with their enchantments and sorceries
questions.explanation: Isaiah 47:12 tells Babylon to stand now with their enchantments and sorceries from youth, hoping to profit or prevail, but this is shown to be futile later in the chapter.

questions.question: Who does Isaiah 47:13 identify as those Babylon should call on for help?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 47:13 lists astrologers, stargazers, and monthly prognosticators as those Babylon relies on for help, indicating their trust in occult practices rather than God.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 47:14, what will happen to those who try to save Babylon with fire?
options: They will be burned and unable to save themselves
They will become leaders over Babylon
They will flee and hide in caves
questions.correctAnswer: They will be burned and unable to save themselves
questions.explanation: Isaiah 47:14 describes those who try to rescue Babylon as stubble burned by fire, unable to deliver themselves or others, showing the futility of their efforts.

questions.question: What is the fate of Babylon’s merchants as stated in Isaiah 47:15?
options: They will wander to their own quarters and not save Babylon
They will unite and protect Babylon
They will be honored as leaders
They will repent and seek God's mercy
questions.correctAnswer: They will wander to their own quarters and not save Babylon
questions.explanation: Isaiah 47:15 states Babylon’s merchants will scatter and none will save her, signifying complete abandonment in her time of judgment.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 47:6 teaches that God's anger led Him to give His people into Babylon's control.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 47:6 clearly states that God was wroth with His people and gave them into Babylon's hand, showing divine judgment as the reason for their captivity.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 47:7 shows Babylon was humble and repentant about its future.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 47:7 reveals Babylon's arrogance, stating 'I shall be a lady forever,' and not considering the latter end, which contradicts humility and repentance.

questions.question: True or False: According to Isaiah 47:8, Babylon confidently believed it would not suffer loss or widowhood.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 47:8 describes Babylon as saying in her heart she will not sit as a widow or know the loss of children, showing her overconfidence.

questions.question: What lesson can believers learn about pride and trust from Isaiah 47:9-10?
options: Trusting in wickedness and pride leads to sudden judgment
Pride brings lasting peace and protection
Trusting sorceries is a way to gain wisdom
Pride is rewarded by God with blessings
questions.correctAnswer: Trusting in wickedness and pride leads to sudden judgment
questions.explanation: Isaiah 47:9-10 teaches that Babylon’s pride and trust in wickedness and enchantments result in sudden loss and judgment, warning believers to avoid such pride and trust in God instead.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 47:11-13 illustrate the futility of relying on occult practices?
options: Evil will come unexpectedly, and sorceries will not save
Occult practices will protect Babylon from all harm
They will bring wisdom and knowledge to Babylon
They will cause Babylon to prosper
questions.correctAnswer: Evil will come unexpectedly, and sorceries will not save
questions.explanation: Verses 11-13 explain that evil and desolation will come suddenly, and despite Babylon’s reliance on sorceries and astrologers, they will not prevail, showing the futility of such trust.

hard.title: Isaiah Chapter 47 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Isaiah Chapter 47.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 47:11, what will come upon Babylon suddenly, without them knowing its origin?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 47:11 states that evil and mischief shall come upon Babylon suddenly, and they will not know from whence it riseth.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 47:12 suggest Babylon should do with their enchantments and sorceries?
options: Stand with them and try to profit
Use them to bless the people
questions.correctAnswer: Stand with them and try to profit
questions.explanation: Isaiah 47:12 commands Babylon to stand with their enchantments and sorceries to see if they may profit or prevail.

questions.question: Who are called to stand up and save Babylon from coming destruction in Isaiah 47:13?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 47:13 mentions astrologers, stargazers, and monthly prognosticators as those who should attempt to save Babylon.

questions.question: What fate does Isaiah 47:14 predict will befall the astrologers and sorcerers of Babylon?
options: They will be like stubble burned by fire
They will be exalted and praised
They will be carried into exile
They will be blinded and silenced
questions.correctAnswer: They will be like stubble burned by fire
questions.explanation: Isaiah 47:14 declares that the astrologers and sorcerers will be like stubble burned by fire, unable to save themselves.

questions.question: In Isaiah 47:15, who will fail to save Babylon despite their long association?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 47:15 says that the merchants, with whom Babylon has labored from youth, will wander each to his quarter and none shall save her.

questions.question: What does the word 'desolation' (Isaiah 47:11) signify in the context of this chapter?
questions.explanation: 'Desolation' in Isaiah 47:11 refers to sudden ruin and abandonment that will come upon Babylon unexpectedly.

questions.question: Which other biblical passage echoes the theme of sudden destruction and inability to save oneself, similar to Isaiah 47:14?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 51:30 also speaks of Babylon’s destruction and the inability of its wise men to save her, echoing Isaiah 47:14’s theme.

questions.question: In Isaiah 47:10, what caused Babylon’s perversion and false confidence?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 47:10 explains that Babylon’s wisdom and knowledge perverted her, leading to false confidence and arrogance.

questions.question: What literary device is primarily used in Isaiah 47:14 when describing the fate of Babylon's astrologers as 'stubble' burned by fire?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 47:14 uses a simile, comparing astrologers to stubble burned by fire using 'as' or 'like' to illustrate their destruction.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 47:8, what false belief did Babylon hold about her future?
options: That she would not sit as a widow or know the loss of children
That she would be destroyed quickly
That she would be conquered by Israel
That she would lose her wealth
questions.correctAnswer: That she would not sit as a widow or know the loss of children
questions.explanation: Isaiah 47:8 states Babylon’s false confidence that she would not become a widow or suffer the loss of children.

questions.question: What is the significance of the title 'The LORD of hosts' given in Isaiah 47:4?
options: It identifies God as the Redeemer and powerful commander of heavenly armies
It refers to a Babylonian deity
It is a title for the king of Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: It identifies God as the Redeemer and powerful commander of heavenly armies
questions.explanation: Isaiah 47:4 explains that 'The LORD of hosts' is the Redeemer’s name, emphasizing God's omnipotence and divine protection of Israel.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 47:7 indicates that Babylon considered the end of her reign and downfall carefully.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 47:7 states that Babylon did not lay these things to heart nor remember the latter end, showing a lack of consideration for her downfall.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 47:6 reveals that God was angry with His people and allowed them to be handed over to Babylon because of their sins.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 47:6 states God’s wrath with His people and that He polluted His inheritance and gave them into Babylon’s hand because of their sins.

questions.question: What Hebrew word concept underlies the term 'enchantments' in Isaiah 47:12, and what does it imply about Babylon’s practices?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'Kesem' translated as 'enchantments' in Isaiah 47:12 implies Babylon practiced witchcraft and occult arts from youth.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage reflects the theme of God’s judgment on proud nations as seen in Isaiah 47?
questions.explanation: Revelation 18 describes the fall of Babylon the Great, echoing Isaiah 47’s themes of judgment and destruction of proud nations.

theological.title: Isaiah Chapter 47 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Isaiah Chapter 47 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 47:1 refer to when mentioning the 'virgin daughter of Babylon'?
questions.explanation: The phrase 'virgin daughter of Babylon' symbolizes a once proud and seemingly untouchable entity that is now being brought low, as seen in Isaiah 47:1, where it states that she shall no longer be called tender and delicate.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 47:3, what will happen to Babylon's nakedness?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 47:3 states that 'Thy nakedness shall be uncovered,' indicating that Babylon's shame will be visible for all to see, symbolizing divine judgment.

questions.question: What title is given to the Lord in Isaiah 47:4?
questions.explanation: In Isaiah 47:4, the Lord is referred to as 'the Holy One of Israel,' emphasizing His holiness and covenant relationship with His people.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 47:6 indicate about Babylon's treatment of God's people?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 47:6 reveals that Babylon 'didst shew them no mercy' and laid a heavy yoke upon God's people, indicating their cruel treatment.

questions.question: What does Babylon claim about its status in Isaiah 47:7?
options: It will be a lady for ever
questions.correctAnswer: It will be a lady for ever
questions.explanation: Isaiah 47:7 states that Babylon said, 'I shall be a lady for ever,' showcasing its pride and false sense of security regarding its power.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 47:10 reveal about Babylon's trust?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 47:10 indicates that Babylon has 'trusted in thy wickedness,' highlighting its reliance on evil rather than on God.

questions.question: What two calamities does Isaiah 47:9 predict for Babylon?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 47:9 warns of impending disaster, predicting 'the loss of children, and widowhood,' indicating severe judgment.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 47:11 indicate about the coming evil upon Babylon?
options: It will be easy to escape
questions.explanation: Isaiah 47:11 states that evil shall come upon Babylon suddenly, indicating that it will catch them off guard.

questions.question: In Isaiah 47:12, what does God challenge Babylon to do with its enchantments?
options: To stand and profit from them
questions.correctAnswer: To stand and profit from them
questions.explanation: Isaiah 47:12 challenges Babylon to 'stand now with thine enchantments' if they believe they can save themselves, highlighting their futility.

questions.question: What is said to happen to Babylon's sorcerers in Isaiah 47:14?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 47:14 describes that the sorcerers will be as stubble, indicating their complete ineffectiveness against God's judgment.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 47:15 imply about Babylon's merchants?
options: They will unite to help Babylon
questions.explanation: Isaiah 47:15 indicates that the merchants will wander and 'none shall save thee,' emphasizing the total abandonment and judgment upon Babylon.

questions.question: What attribute of God is highlighted in Isaiah 47:4?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 47:4 refers to the Lord as 'the Holy One of Israel,' emphasizing His divine attribute of holiness, distinct from all sin.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 47:11 connect to the broader theme of divine justice?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 47:11 emphasizes that evil will come upon Babylon unexpectedly, reflecting God's justice in punishing unrepentant sin.

questions.question: What is the combined teaching of verses 8 and 10 regarding Babylon's self-assurance?
questions.explanation: Verses 8 and 10 illustrate Babylon's pride and self-assurance ('I am, and none else beside me') which ultimately leads to its downfall as they ignore the warning of impending judgment.

questions.question: What does the combination of verses 6 and 9 reveal about God's view of Babylon's actions?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 47:6 and 9 combined reveal that God views Babylon's actions toward His people as cruel, having shown no mercy and leading to severe consequences.
